model: Securities broker FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, regulatory-capital retention charged as capex, perpetual-bond and NCI distributions charged in the tax line, pro forma for the Dongxing/Cinda merger by absorption

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E PRO FORMA total revenue and other income (IFRS gross basis: fee and commission + interest income + investment income + other), RMB m. CICC standalone: H1 2026 actual 26,440 (+43.7% YoY, interim p.534) + H2 2026E 23,500 (H2 2025 actual 22,115 = FY2025 40,518 - H1 2025 18,403; A-share turnover stayed strong into H2 but HK indices fell 11-19% in H1 and the H share has derated from its 52-week high toward its low, so H2 is held just above H2 2025 and below H1 2026) = ~49,900. Dongxing Securities + Cinda Securities FY2026E on the same gross basis ~14,000 (estimate: their CAS operating revenue ~RMB10bn grossed to IFRS at the ~1.4x ratio CICC's own IFRS revenue bears to its CAS operating revenue; NOT in the extracted filings -- see merger block). Combined ~63,900, rounded to 64,000.
inputs.share_count_basis: PRO FORMA post-merger: 4,827.257m CICC A+H shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim note 44(a), unchanged since the 2020 A-share IPO) + 3,102.6m new A shares to be issued to Dongxing (3,228.9m shares x 0.4376 = 1,413.0m) and Cinda (3,243.0m shares x 0.5210 = 1,689.6m) share-exchange shareholders (ratios: interim p.2945; target share counts from their own registers, not in this folder's filings). Cross-check: 3,102.6m x CICC A-share reference price ~RMB36.7 = RMB113.9bn, matching the RMB113.85bn deal value reported in the press. Dissenting-shareholder cash options (put to Shenwan Hongyuan/Industrial Securities/Jianyin) could trim the issued count marginally; ignored. Held FLAT thereafter: SBC-zero, no buyback programme, no further issuance assumed. A and H shares carry identical economic rights, so the per-share value applies to the H share. UNCERTAINTY: the exact post-merger count will only be confirmed in the completion announcement / FY2026 annual report -- refresh it then.
inputs.debt_cash_note: Securities firm: debt securities issued (~RMB122bn corporate bonds + RMB17.3bn perpetuals classified as liabilities at 30 June 2026, interim p.5502/8508), repos, interbank placements and accounts payable to brokerage clients are operating funding for the trading, margin-financing and market-making books; cash and bank balances are mostly client money and liquidity reserves. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route and nothing is bridged after the flows. The CSV's total_debt (162,927 at H1 2026) is balance-sheet leverage, not valuation net debt.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E PRO FORMA FCFE = ordinary net profit 19,200 (PBT 24,000 at 37.5% x (1 - 20% tax/NCI/perpetual-distribution rate)) LESS equity retained to grow the pro forma ordinary equity base (~RMB163bn) by 3% = 4,900. Reported OCF - capex (H1 2026: 1,470 - 249 = 1,221; FY2025: 41,647 - 765 = 40,881; FY2023: -3,882) swings with FVTPL and margin-client balances and is not an earnings proxy. Standalone CICC FY2026E: PBT ~18,000 (H1 actual 10,208 + H2E ~7,750), ordinary NI ~14,400 after tax ~17%, NCI and ~750 of perpetual coupons.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: no share-based payment scheme or share-award trust disclosed in the FY2018-FY2025 annual reports or the H1 2026 interim; ShareRepurchases 0 every period; basic = diluted EPS. House and street bases coincide; band_position is degenerate (null).
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; CICC reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1735 at 2026-10-22, Yahoo Finance chart API. The Shanghai A share (601995.SS) closed at CNY 31.22 = HKD 36.6 on 2026-10-22 against the H share's close the same day (current_price), a ~104% A/H premium (A-share brokers trade at ~2x book, H shares at <1x), so the dual listing is a premium reference, not a parity check. The merger share-exchange is priced in A shares, which is why it is dilutive to the H share on book and earnings per share (see merger block).
inputs.fy0: FY2026E pro forma (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: CICC H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate + full-year estimate for Dongxing and Cinda)
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (CICC register) + merger exchange ratios fixed May 2026; completion pending
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 11.0% in CNY (the flows' currency): CNY 10-year government yield ~1.8% + China equity risk premium ~6.5% x beta ~1.4 for a securities firm with 7.7x operating leverage on ordinary equity (interim p.2087), 39.6% of assets in FVTPL/derivatives, and revenue that swung 41.5bn (FY2021) -> 31.4bn (FY2024) -> 40.5bn (FY2025) with the market cycle. Sits between the 10.5% used for the large Chinese banks (0998.HK, 3618.HK) and the 11.5% used for the smaller HK broker 1788.HK; Central Huijin control and no credit book argue for the lower end, cyclicality and merger integration for the higher. Bull 10.5% (merger de-risked, scale lowers funding cost), bear 12.0% (integration disruption on top of a market downturn).
inputs.lease_treatment: IFRS 16 lease payments (~RMB950m/yr principal) sit inside the pre-tax margin via depreciation of right-of-use assets and lease interest; no separate lease charge and lease liabilities (RMB3.7bn) are not treated as debt. Charged once, in the margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests of RMB8,313m at 30 June 2026 (up from 2,331m at FY2025 and 274m at FY2024) are NOT merger consolidation: the equity statement (interim p.7125) shows RMB6,000m of perpetual subordinated bonds issued by subsidiary CICC Wealth Management in H1 2026 (26 CICC WMS Y1/Y2, interim p.5068/5085) booked as NCI, plus a RMB98m capital contribution; the Dongxing/Cinda targets were not consolidated at 30 June 2026 (no cash from acquisition of subsidiaries in H1 2026, interim p.7260). Distributions to those NCI perpetuals (RMB186m in H1 2026) and to the parent's RMB29.8bn equity-classified perpetuals (RMB563m paid in H1 2026, RMB375m accrued, interim note 18) are charged in the cash_tax_rate_path on top of income tax, so FCFE is to ORDINARY shareholders. This corrects the Analysis JSON's reading that NCI rose because the merger began landing in Q2 2026.
inputs.notes: MODEL: securities-broker FCFE capitalised at the cost of equity, run through the component engine (revenue x pre-tax margin = 'EBITDA'; income tax + NCI + perpetual-bond distributions as the tax line; equity retained for regulatory capital/balance-sheet growth as 'capex'; D&A, SBC, leases and working capital zero; net debt zero; terminal Gordon on FCFE at CoE). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: a securities firm is a leveraged financial whose reported OCF and 'net debt' are trading-book noise, so the owner-FCF route is meaningless; the same convention as the folder's bank (0998.HK, 2016.HK, 3618.HK) and broker (1788.HK) valuations. BASIS: PRO FORMA for the merger by absorption of Dongxing Securities and Cinda Securities (SSE M&A committee approval 27 Aug 2026, CSRC acceptance 12 Jun 2026 and approval Sep 2026, A shares suspended from 15 Sep 2026 for completion) -- by the valuation date the deal is approved and unconditional, so the H-share holder owns 1/7,930m of the combined firm, not 1/4,827m of standalone CICC. The targets' figures are estimates from their own public disclosures, not from this folder's filings; the merger block gives the standalone comparison. Book value per share: use total equity attributable (RMB134,060m) LESS other equity instruments (RMB29,800m) = RMB104,260m ordinary / 4,827m = RMB21.60 standalone (interim p.560 uses the same definition); pro forma tangible ordinary book ~RMB163bn / 7,930m = ~RMB20.6 (goodwill of ~RMB60bn created by issuing shares at the A-share price is excluded). The H share at current_price (~RMB15.3 at fx_rate) trades at ~0.71x standalone and ~0.74x pro forma tangible book, ~5x FY2026E standalone EPS and ~6.3x pro forma EPS.

merger.status: Merger by absorption and share exchange of Dongxing Securities (601198.SS) and Cinda Securities (601059.SS); board 18 May 2026, EGM/class meetings 8 Jun 2026, SSE acceptance 12 Jun 2026, SSE M&A Review Committee approval 27 Aug 2026, CSRC approval Sep 2026; A shares of all three suspended from 15 Sep 2026 pending completion. Treated as certain.
merger.target_estimates_note: Dongxing (3,228.9m shares) and Cinda (3,243.0m shares) are not in this folder's filings. Estimates used: combined FY2026E PBT ~RMB6.0bn, ordinary net profit ~RMB4.8bn, tangible net assets ~RMB52bn (Dongxing ~RMB29bn, Cinda ~RMB23bn), total assets ~RMB200bn; combined FY2024 actual net profit was ~RMB3.1bn (Dongxing ~1.65bn, Cinda ~1.45bn) and FY2025/26 are bull-market years. These are the least certain inputs in the file; replace with the FY2026 annual report's consolidated figures and the completion announcement's share count.
merger.dilution_note: Consideration ~RMB113.85bn (A-share priced) for ~RMB52bn of tangible book and ~RMB4.8bn of earnings = ~2.2x P/TBV, ~24x P/E, against CICC's own H share at ~0.7x and ~5x. Per H share the deal adds ~47% to tangible book and ~33% to ordinary earnings for 64% more shares: pro forma TBV/share falls ~11% (RMB21.6 -> ~20.6 before H2 2026 retention) and EPS ~19%. Standalone CICC on the same base/CoE would value ~15-20% higher per share than the pro forma number; the gap is the price the H holder pays for a merger struck at A-share valuations. Synergies ('1+2>3') are in the bull margin path, integration cost in the bear.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: long-run revenue trend (FY2020-FY2025 revenue CAGR 3.3%, FY2022-25 3.2%) and the terminal rate; equity CAGR is not used because it is inflated by retained earnings at a ~12% payout and RMB28.8bn of perpetual-bond issuance
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 11.2% (8.4% ex-perpetuals) vs revenue 3.3% and EPS 3.3%: the equity base has compounded 2.5-3x faster than revenue or EPS, i.e. ROE has been diluted by retention (FY2021 14.6% -> FY2024 5.5% -> FY2025 9.4%). Revenue, EPS and net income are measured FY2020->FY2025 and FY2022->FY2025 (IFRS total revenue and other income; EPS basic RMB; 'fcf' CAGRs are net profit attributable, because reported FCF is trading-book noise: FY2020 -34,199, FY2022 +56,375, FY2023 -3,882, FY2025 +40,881).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF and its CAGR are not computable for a securities firm; net profit attributable to shareholders (FY2020 7,207 -> FY2025 9,791; FY2022 7,598 -> FY2025 9,791) stands in. FY2021 was the prior cycle peak (revenue 41,461, NI 10,778); FY2025 regained it and H1 2026 (NI 8,199, +89%) is tracking a new record.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 -8% and FY2028 -3%: FY2026E is a record (A-share daily turnover +97% YoY in H1 2026, HK IPO proceeds +93%); the prior peak FY2021 was followed by -11% and -8%. Then 4% fading to 3%: balance-sheet growth of the enlarged firm (margin financing, market-making, OTC derivatives) plus AUM-linked fees, in line with the FY2020-25 revenue CAGR of 3.3% plus a modest scale/synergy lift.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin on IFRS gross revenue. History: FY2021 32.3% (peak), FY2022 24.6%, FY2023 20.2% (trough), FY2024 21.7%, FY2025 28.9%, H1 2026 38.6%, FY2026E pro forma 37.5%. Base steps down to 29% as turnover normalises and compensation ratios reset, then edges to 30% as merger cost synergies (branch, IT and licence rationalisation) come through -- mid-cycle plus 1-2pt of scale.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to grow pro forma ordinary equity (~RMB163bn at end-FY2026E) with the balance sheet: 3% in FY2027 (post-peak consolidation), 4% FY2028-31, 3.5% FY2032-33, 3% FY2034-36, i.e. retention / revenue = 0.03 x 163,000 / 58,880 = 8.3% in FY2027 and ~0.04 x equity / revenue = 11.8% thereafter. This is what CSRC net-capital, risk-coverage (168.5% at H1 2026, down from 183%) and capital-leverage (10.4%, down from 12.2%) ratios require if assets grow with revenue; CICC's actual payout has been only 9-15% of profit, so the modelled FCFE (55-70% of ordinary NI) is a distributable capacity, not the dividend. Terminal ordinary equity ~RMB225bn, terminal ROE ~7.9%.
base.tax_rationale: Of PBT: income tax ~16-19% (FY2025 16.3%, H1 2026 19.0%; statutory 25% less tax-exempt fund distributions and government-bond interest) + NCI ~0.7% (including coupons on the RMB8bn of subsidiary perpetuals) + parent perpetual-bond coupons ~3% (RMB29.8bn at ~2.3% = ~RMB700m) = ~20%, held flat. Coupons are fixed in RMB so the share drifts down as PBT grows; ignored (conservative).
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 11.0% - 3.0% = 12.9x FCFE; the 18x cap does not bind. Implied terminal P/B ~0.6x on terminal ROE ~7.9% vs CoE 11%, consistent with (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) and with where CICC H has traded through the cycle (0.4-1.2x).
base.narrative: Normal cycle: FY2026E record fades 10% over two years, then the enlarged CICC grows revenue 3-4% a year with its balance sheet at a ~29-30% pre-tax margin, retains ~3-4% of equity a year for net capital and distributes the rest. Merger completes on the fixed ratios with modest cost synergies and no serious integration disruption.

bull.growth_rationale: No post-peak reset: China/HK capital markets stay active (STAR/sci-tech listings, HK IPO pipeline, RMB internationalisation), the enlarged balance sheet grows margin and market-making books 6%, cross-selling of Dongxing/Cinda clients into CICC wealth and IB delivers the '1+2>3' revenue synergy.
bull.margin_rationale: Holds near the FY2026E level: operating leverage on a larger platform plus cost synergies; 33% is just above the FY2021 peak (32.3%), i.e. sustained prosperity, not a new structural level.
bull.capex_rationale: Equity retained to grow ordinary equity 4%, 5%, 6%, 6%, 6%, 5%, 5%, 4%, 4%, 4% from RMB163bn -- faster growth needs more regulatory capital. Terminal ROE ~10%.
bull.narrative: The merger makes CICC a top-3 Chinese investment bank at a 33% margin with ROE back above 10%; the H-share discount narrows toward 1x tangible book. Roughly the sell-side case (JPM HKD28.5, GS HKD28.15 targets).

bear.growth_rationale: FY2022-24-style downturn after the FY2026 peak (revenue fell 24% from FY2021 to FY2024), compounded by integration disruption and continued US-China listing friction; then low-single-digit growth.
bear.margin_rationale: FY2023 trough was 20.2%; bear bottoms at 21% in FY2028 with integration costs and compensation stickiness, recovering only to 24% (below the 2021-25 average of ~25.5%).
bear.capex_rationale: Equity still retained (2%, 2.5%, then 3% a year to FY2033, 2.5% after) because regulatory ratios are closest to their floors exactly when markets fall -- the retention does not stop in a downturn, which is why ROE falls to ~5% and FCFE to ~half of NI. Terminal ROE ~5.3%.
bear.tax_rationale: Perpetual coupons are fixed in RMB, so they take a larger share of a smaller PBT: ~21%.
bear.narrative: Market turnover halves from the 2026 peak, integration of two full-licence brokerages drags on for years, ROE settles at 5-6% against a 12% cost of equity and the H share stays at 0.3-0.4x book, where it traded in 2024.

scenario_narratives.base: Normal post-peak cycle for the merged CICC/Dongxing/Cinda: revenue -10% over FY2027-28, then 3-4% growth at a 29-30% pre-tax margin; 3-4% of equity retained a year for net capital; CoE 11%, terminal growth 3%, terminal ROE ~8% and P/B ~0.6x.
scenario_narratives.bull: Prolonged capital-markets upcycle and real merger synergies: 33% margin, 4-6% growth, ROE ~10%, CoE 10.5%, terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2022-24-style downturn plus integration disruption: revenue -26% over two years, margin trough 21%, ROE ~5%, CoE 12%, terminal growth 2.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (above the 25% house default): FY2026E is a record year for a business whose revenue fell 24% peak-to-trough last cycle, the merger closes at the top of that cycle with two full-licence brokerages to integrate at once, and regulatory ratios (risk coverage 168.5%, capital leverage 10.4%) are already drifting toward their floors. Bull 25%: the CSRC's consolidation policy and the enlarged franchise give a genuine route to >10% ROE, and the sell side is there. Base 45%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A securities firm is valued on the cash it can distribute to ordinary shareholders after funding the regulatory capital its balance sheet needs, discounted at the cost of equity; reported operating cash flow and 'net debt' are trading-book noise and are not used. The valuation is pro forma for the approved Dongxing/Cinda merger, which is dilutive to the H share on tangible book (~-11%) and earnings per share (~-19%) because it is struck at A-share valuations ~2x the H share's. The H share's ~0.7x tangible book and ~5x peak EPS already discount a cyclical reset; what it does not discount is a long downturn plus integration drag, which is why the bear carries 30%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Target financials (Dongxing, Cinda) and the post-merger share count are estimates from outside this folder's filings; the FY2026 annual report and completion announcement will reset base_revenue, last_fcf and shares_outstanding
Cyclicality: FY2026E revenue and margin are at a record; every scenario assumes some reset, and the timing of the next downturn dominates the base/bear split
Integration of two separately licensed, listed brokerages at once (IT, risk control, branch network, personnel) could depress margins for longer than the bear's two years

Distributable FCFE is modelled at 55-70% of ordinary earnings but CICC has paid out only 9-15%; if retention stays at that level without proportionate balance-sheet growth, ROE keeps diluting and the terminal P/B falls
RMB29.8bn of parent perpetuals plus RMB8bn of subsidiary perpetuals rank ahead of ordinary equity; further issuance to fund growth would raise the fixed charge in the tax line
A/H premium of ~104%: the model values the share on CNY flows converted at spot; a narrowing or widening of the premium moves the H share independently of fundamentals
No SBC and no buyback: house and street values coincide, so the band is degenerate (band_position null)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 16.91-23.72 HKD. A-share reference 601995.SS same source, same day.
data_sources.financials: research/3908.HK/Reports/3908.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, CNY millions) FY2017-H1 FY2026; H1 2026 interim report (3908.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt) for PBT, tax, NCI, perpetuals, share capital and merger terms; FY2025 annual report for dividend policy and FY2025 lines.
data_sources.qualitative: research/3908.HK/Reports/3908.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-23); its reading that the H1 2026 NCI rise reflects merger consolidation is corrected in inputs.nci_treatment (it is subsidiary perpetual bonds).
